full.description: This is a gross specimen image of the gastrointestinal system, specifically the small intestine. It shows marked thickening of the bowel wall along with creeping fat in the surrounding mesentery. The mucosal surface displays characteristic cobblestone-like changes and ulcerations. These features are classically associated with Crohn disease.

random.description: This is a gross pathology specimen of an organ, likely representing a portion of the small intestine or bowel with attached adipose tissue. The mucosal surface shows prominent folds and abnormal thickening, with some nodular changes and ulceration visible. These findings are characteristic of severe inflammatory or neoplastic conditions affecting the gastrointestinal tract, such as Crohn's disease or a malignancy. The thickened wall and surrounding fat creeping indicate transmural involvement typical of chronic inflammatory bowel disease.
